DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: unitary penetrating warhead
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: A WDU-36-class unitary charge: a lighter, tougher case with more explosive efficiency than the old Scorer warhead, and enough penetration to open a roof before it detonates.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: hard-target penetrator
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: A dense tungsten penetrator that punches through thick roofs and overhead mountain before detonating inside, in the bunker-buster role the Tomahawk family also carries. Underground shelters stop being protection.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: terrain-matching guidance
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: Terrain contour matching and scene matching in the TERCOM/DSMAC tradition: the missile flies a survey-grade route and corrects itself against the ground, giving very tight dispersion. It cannot be re-targeted in flight and has no terminal guidance at all, so a target that moves away is simply missed.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: two-way datalink
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: A satellite datalink of the Block IV kind: the missile can be re-targeted while in flight and even loiter, and when it reaches the target map the game pauses and you pick the impact point yourself. The most accurate option, and the only one that lets a moving target be chased mid-flight.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: anti-ship radar seeker
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: An active radar seeker built for moving targets: ships and any other mobile base on the world map. It keeps re-aiming while the target keeps moving and does so more often than a normal seeker; the missile still misses if the target leaves its remaining range.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: turbofan sustainer
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: A small turbofan in the F107 class, burning liquid fuel at altitude. Far more efficient than a rocket motor and much quieter on radar than a booster, at the cost of speed.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: extended-range turbofan
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: A fuel-optimised turbofan with a larger tank. The longest reach of any cruise configuration, but the slowest to arrive and the most expensive to build.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: solid rocket booster
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: A jettisonable solid booster that shoves the missile to speed and then burns out. Very fast and very obvious: range suffers because the booster case and propellant eat into the airframe budget.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: no payload
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: No secondary payload. The unitary warhead and the fuel tank get the whole airframe.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: submunition dispenser
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: A dispenser of combined-effects bomblets in the TLAM-D tradition: the missile opens up over the target and scatters a cluster of small charges across the area instead of one concentrated blast.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: graphite filament payload
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: A carbon-fibre payload in the Kit-2 tradition: instead of blast, it shorts out the electrical grid around the impact, disabling powered buildings and stunning mechanoids over a wide radius.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: decoy payload
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: Radar reflectors and a signal augmenter in place of a secondary charge. On enemy radar the missile looks twice its size: it is detected earlier, and air defences that rank threats by size engage it first. It does no extra damage.

DMSE.MissilePartDef.label: chaff dispenser
DMSE.MissilePartDef.description: A heavier chaff and streamer dispenser for the cruise airframe. Each bundle can break an enemy fire-control lock; there are more bundles than the light dispenser carries, but they are still expended one by one and never reloaded in flight.
